newsitem.title: UK: Panamaxes continue to feature in dry cargo market.
newsitem.headline: Panamaxes continue to feature in dry cargo market.

text.p: Panamax tonnage continued to enjoy the spotlight in the dry cargo market on Tuesday, although some brokers believed early loading positions in the U.S. Gulf were a shade weaker.
They said a few vessels on these dates would have to accept slightly lower rates than last fixed, but beyond mid-November prospects for owners still appeared encouraging.
In the Pacific Japanese charterers were described as 'feeding in force' on Panamax, and firmer fixtures were noted for trips and short period charters.

Capers once again featured in the Atlantic grain trades and there appeared to be a significant rise in rates in the Pacific. Handy-sizes are in strong demand in the U.S. Gulf area, but elsewhere there is little change reported yet in this category.

GRAIN - Iranian charterers are believed to have covered two Caper vessels from the St. Lawrence. These were Akova for 90,000 tonnes wheat to Iran for November, loading at $17.00 basis 2-1 and Haralaos 112,000 tonnes dwt delivery prompt Passero for a trip via St. Lawrence to Iran at $9,000 daily.

Continental are understood to have taken a Caper for 80,000 tonnes wheat St. Lawrence/Dammam at close to $17.50 basis 2-1. Meanwhile, Cargill have now finally covered Konavle for 60,000 tonnes HSS U.S. Gulf/Continent at a firm lumpsum equivalent to $13.50 for Nov 15/22 (this fixture was first rumoured last Friday).

However, South Korean charterers are said to have failed with Andre tonnage for 52/54,000 tonnes HSS U.S. Gulf/Japan for Nov 15/30 at $22.75 and European charterers with Bulfracht tonnage for Dec at $23.00, both basis no combo.
Tomis Glory 65,275 tonnes dwt was linked with HMM delivery Continent trip via U.S. Gulf to the Far East at $11,000 daily.

Despite various Chinese operators enquiring for Panamaxes for November grain or fertilizer stems to the Far East, brokers are uncertain how great a volume of business there is in the pipeline before the end of the year.
Few other new grain orders were seen today - Italgrani quoted 50/55,000 tonnes HSS St. Lawrence/Rotterdam for Nov 22/27 and Cargill 40/50,000 tonnes barley Brisbane/Saudi Red Sea for Nov 4/9.

But at the same time the fixtures which did emerge have nearly all been at steady or better levels. Handy-size fixture turnover was poor, but Andre covered 25,000 tonnes HSS U.S. Gulf/Aqaba for mid-Nov on private terms, possibly at a little over $27.00.

MINERALS/FERTS - Japanese charterers were busy covering Panamaxes delivery Far East for short period timecharters. In addition, Eastern Queen 70,197 tonnes dwt for three to five months at $10,150 daily, Glory Hope 68,158 tonnes dwt was rumoured taken for a similar period at $10,000 daily and Drin 73,087 tonnes dwt at $10,250, both with early Nov delivery.
Merchant Pioneer 69,763 tonnes dwt which sailed Kobe, direction Nopac, on Oct 25 was believed booked for three to five months at close to $10,500 daily by European charterers.
Perhaps the steepest rate jump seen today was Cockerill's fixture of Highlander for 140,000 tonnes coal two ports Queensland/Rotterdam and Antwerp for Nov 15/30 at $11.50.
La Pampa 139,000 tonnes dwt was fixed delivery South Korea for a Pacific round on private terms.

Fertilizer business was covered on subjects in the Atlantic by Unitramp with Deerpool 65,163 tonnes dwt delivery Morocco trip West Coast Mexico at $12,000 daily. Unnamed charterers were reported to have covered 25,000 tonnes phosphate Tampa/Karachi at $32.00 for November shipment.
HANDY-SIZES - Lakers continued to command substantial rates. UBT paid between $9,000 and $9,250 daily for the 1979-built Anax 30,000 tonnes dwt delivery Norway trip via Lakes redelivery Montreal.
On the other hand the Far East was relatively weak - Aristotelis 23,000 tonnes dwt was fixed by Furness Withy delivery Tasmania trip Continent at only about $4,250 daily.
